quest.title: The Seeker of a Meteor Shower
quest.description: Back in Inazuma, Yoimiya is preparing for a romantic journey...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Have you packed all your things? Make sure you've brought the onigiri and rice cakes your mother prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I have them all! They're going to last me days!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Take care of yourselves while I'm out, and make sure you remind Mom to take her medicine on time.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If running the store gets a bit too much, take some time off and wait for me to return.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Oh, Yoimiya, your mother and I got so worried when we heard that you were going so far abroad.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: We've never left the country, so we don't know how outlanders might view us Inazumans, or if they'd even be willing to speak to us...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, relax! Outlanders are friendly and warm!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Look at Thoma from the Yashiro Commission. He's originally from Mondstadt, but everyone thinks he's a top-tier guy!

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: A mop-tier? What mop? Oh, do you mean the broken one at home? I just fixed it today, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No, I said "top," not "mop"! You know, Thoma even sent us some wine from his homeland not too long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't heard this kind of friendly banter in a while, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, hey you two! It's been a long time, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're as peppy as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, I'm excited because I'm going on a trip soon!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Many things have changed. Lots of outlanders have come to Inazuma, and lots of Inazumans have gone out as well.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You two have been adventuring all over Teyvat, so you might not be able to understand, but for us, this is a long-awaited chance to go out and fulfill our dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, the Sakoku Decree is gone.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Ah, I remember you two. You're Yoimiya's friends, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Word of your incredible accomplishments has spread throughout Inazuma. My daughter's a big fan of yours — she said she'd love to be like you two.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, c'mon, Dad... Who's never dreamed of becoming a hero?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've done some heroic feats yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Aw, thanks, but I'm just your average artisan. The quiet life suits me better.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But if an opportunity presents itself, why not try to show your stuff, right?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Alright, did you two come over today to order some fireworks?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh! Sorry, sorry, I got carried away.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: While I'm gone, Dad's in charge of making fireworks. You've seen how skilled he is, so there's nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no, we aren't here to do business or anything. We just happened to be passing by!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, so we're all here with time to spare. What a treat!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: In that case, let's chat some more! I'm not in a rush, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! So, where are you planning to go?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No clue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hahaha! I say that, but I do have a travel goal: to see Teyvat's grandest meteor shower.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But I don't know when or where it'll happen, so I figured I can search while I travel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That's it? No details? Nothing?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Not right now, since this meteor shower was originally something like a family legend.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: A long time ago, the Naganoharas were inspired to create new fireworks after watching such a meteor shower.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Dad says that inspiration is a combination of what you see and what you know. Different people can see the same thing but have different thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Inazuma today is completely different from how it was in the past. If I can see this meteor shower, I'm sure I'll be able to come up with a new kind of firework.

choices.text: Meteors and fireworks...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I know, right? Of course, my main reason is that I want to go and look outside Inazuma, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No need to be shy about it! You gotta play hard when you get the chance!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: You know, you're right, Paimon! Is it just me, or have you gotten wiser since we first met?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon loves being friends with you since you say such nice things!

choices.text: Since you're going out to play regardless...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Sumeru... I've heard of it. It has a ton of trees, a super impressive school, and a massive desert!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's also a division of the school that specializes in studying the stars.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, and everyone there is really smart, so Paimon's sure you'll get some answers from them about the meteor shower!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Really? But, won't research people make fun of me or something if I ask them about a legend?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We won't know if something's real or not unless we ask! Don't worry, we've got solid connections in there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {M#he}{F#she} does, anyway...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Wouldn't I be taking up your time, though? I doubt this was in your schedule...

choices.text: It's fine. This way, your parents can be at ease.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Relax, Yoimiya. You've helped us plenty of times before.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Haha, alright! Then I accept your offer! Let's have some fun in Sumeru!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Dad, you can have more peace of mind now that I'm traveling with them, right?

response.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
response.text: Hm? Ah, yes, your mother and I will be much more at ease.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Remember, you two also need to take care of yourselves! I'll be back soon.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Okay, let's head to Ritou and catch a boat there.

choices.text: I'll be your guide.
Why not make Sumeru your first stop?
They do have some similarities.

talks.objective: Head to the dock in Ritou

dialogues.speaker: During the Journey at Sea
dialogues.text: You board a passenger ship bound for Port Ormos, enjoying the lovely ocean views along the way.

dialogues.speaker: During the Journey at Sea
dialogues.text: Yoimiya listens with rapt attention as you tell her of the events following the Vision Hunt Decree and of your various adventures in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: During the Journey at Sea
dialogues.text: The long voyage ends before you know it...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow, so this is Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That tree's huge... Is the port built on top of it?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: And this place is amazing! It's way bigger than Ritou's port! There are also a lot more stores here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, there's more cool stuff for you to see, don't you worry!

choices.text: Port Ormos also took my breath away when I first arrived.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: This place is awesome! I had heard people describe it, but nothing beats seeing a place for yourself...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: If I hadn't seen the port with my own eyes, I could never have imagined such a place.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: So, the school you were talking about... the Akademiya? Is it here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope. We have to head north from here and follow the river to reach Sumeru City.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Sumeru City, huh... I guess it's even more impressive than here?

choices.text: They each have their own highlights.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Looking forward to it! Heehee, I'm so excited!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Whatever the case, why don't we go to Sumeru City?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, I'm so excited that I don't even know what I should be doing anymore!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The important thing about going on a trip is to enjoy yourself! You don't have to think so hard.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How about we walk around here with you?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I'm just worried that if we don't get down to business soon, I'll take up too much of your time.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hehe, but if you insist... then let's look around!

choices.text: The city has an even bigger tree.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Even bigger!? Oh, I wonder if it's as grand as Sangonomiya Shrine...

choices.text: It's a land of neverending theses.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: The...ses? Um, I don't know much about them, but they sound like something that's a cause for serious anxiety.

choices.text: Welcome to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: Welcome to Acara Crafts! Feel free to have a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow, what are these? They're so cute!

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: This is our current best-seller, the Aranara Carving.

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: Their designs are based on the fairy tales that circulate amongst children, so they're very popular with them.

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: Miss, are you from Inazuma? This would be a great gift for you to bring back home.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ooh, I know about Aranara! You two told me about them on the ship. I didn't think they'd be so cute! No wonder the kids like 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Ooh, they're all so pretty. Lemme take a better look...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knew Yoimiya would like this kind of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But even she might have a hard time seeing a real Aranara...

choices.text: They don't like being disturbed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Sorry Yoimiya, but we need to keep our promise to the Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, Paimon doesn't think Yoimiya would mind too much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Her world's already chock-full of imaginary creatures.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I think I'll get this one... ooh! That one, and the other two that you showed me earlier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You're buying that many?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yep! I'm going to give them out to Saika and the others. They're going to love them! Oh, and these carvings can also be used as prizes in matches against the Arataki Gang.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: They'd also look great lined up by the window. Think about it — you wake up, and the first thing you see are these adorable critters.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Wouldn't they brighten up your entire day?

choices.text: Let me cover some of the cost.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hehe, okay, thanks! In that case, you take your pick, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll go with this one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...For some reason, Paimon thinks it kinda looks like you, Yoimiya.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Now that you mention it, it kinda does!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: "Hello, Nara Paimon. My name is Aramiya!" Plip-plod, plip-plod.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Is that how they talk? Hope I remembered correctly, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was really good! Wow, great memory. We only talked about Aranara that one time on the boat.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: That's because they're so interesting! I'm pretty good at remembering those kinds of things.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could you please package these up for Aramiya?

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: Of course. Thank you for your patronage!

response.speaker: Fayez
response.text: You all are an entertaining bunch. I hope you enjoy your time here in Sumeru!

choices.text: They start your day on the right foot.
That's why we told her they're from fairy tales.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow, this market is even busier than the one in Port Ormos.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is Treasures Street. Up from here is the Akademiya... Oh! And in that tree trunk is the Grand Bazaar. They're both pretty special places.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I just saw a group of people come down, and they were all wearing the same outfit. Is that the Akademiya's uniform?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. They also wear hats with different designs, depending on which Darshan they're in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For example, we'll be looking for someone from Rtawahist. They know a lot about stars and stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Does this mean that you need uniforms like those to get in and out of the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon doesn't think so...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is something worrying you, Yoimiya?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Um, won't we stick out if we go in like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So even you get shy, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No, no, that's not what I meant. Let's pretend you're an Akademiya student, hard at work.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Then in comes a bunch of outlanders in strange clothes who gawk and run around everywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon kinda gets what you mean.

choices.text: We'll be a bit distracting, won't we?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I don't think we have to be too self-conscious, but it's still something to keep in mind.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Why don't we look around here first? I've been wanting to see the "Zubayr Theater," anyway.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: As for the Akademiya... let's go once I get myself a set of Sumeru-style clothes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, but Paimon thinks you're overthinking it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll find you a good tailor later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nilou might have some good recommendations!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Hehe, sounds good. If we can watch a performance of hers while we're at it, that'd be even better!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Alright, I'll be looking around here. I'm leaving the meteor shower inquiry to you two. Thanks a lot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem! We'll be right back.

choices.text: We might even attract the matra's attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what we need to do is to make Yoimiya believe that the meteor shower is really happening, and be super convincing at how we sell it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Complete some challenges, and then reap the rewards.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... If Paimon wanted to go see a meteor shower, the things Paimon would focus on the most would be...

choices.text: The start time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, exactly! We'll say we're trying to figure these two things out, but we'll actually be bringing Yoimiya around to see the sights and enjoy local food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Well, easier said than done. We can't be too strict with our pretext, but we can't be sloppy with it either, or she'll see through it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It'd be best if we could take a unique approach to making it fantastical, just like a real fairy tale. Hmm, this is gonna be hard...

choices.text: This reminds me of the Plane of Euthymia...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right. Um, don't people also talk about wishing on a shooting star?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we used wishes as the center of our story...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A meteor shower is something summoned by people's wishes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah, that sounds great! Alright then, we need a specific wishing spot, or else the sky would be full of meteor showers.

choices.text: We need a certain device to find this location.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And then while we're supposedly finding or making this device, we'll go around and have fun and eat good food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heehee, this is shaping up to be the perfect plot!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, the device can be anything and the location can be wherever. As long as we get Yoimiya to enter the dream at night, things will be fine.

choices.text: You're getting ever smarter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This isn't about being smart, it's about being a good duo! The idea was yours, anyway. Paimon just knows what you wanna say!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright, let's go. Yoimiya's probably sick of waiting for us.

choices.text: Your brain always works so well when food comes up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's nothing wrong with that! You should know Paimon pretty well by now.

choices.text: Just like how Rtawahist requires their observational instruments.
When stars symbolizing wishes appeared in the sky.
...And the perfect vantage point.

talks.objective: Return to Treasures Street and look for Yoimiya

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Thanks so much! If it weren't for your help, I would've gotten lost already.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: It's no problem. I'll be heading home, then.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Just a minute, wait! This is for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: This is an Aranara Carving I bought in Port Ormos. I heard it's very popular with kids, so here, have one.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: It's alright, I didn't do much, really...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's fine, take it! C'mon, just look at its big, happy smile!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You can display it at home or hang it on your wheelchair. It'll cheer you up.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That might sound silly to you... Like, why do you have to be happy just because it is?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But that's the magic of a smile. If you don't believe me, try it. Look at it a few times every day, and you'll understand.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: ...Actually, I feel like I already do. You love talking, and you love smiling, too.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: I just don't understand why you're so... positive. I've never met anyone like you before.

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm not very good with words. But since you say so, I'll accept your gift.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Want me to take you home?

dialogues.speaker: Avin
dialogues.text: It's okay, I can head back myself.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The child in the wheelchair leaves.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, great timing, you two!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who was that kid?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, her? Her name is Avin. I saw that she was looking quite forlorn, so I wanted to make sure she wasn't feeling left out or alone.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: She was pretty shy at first, but I explained that I just arrived in Sumeru and had gotten lost, so I needed someone to help guide me...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: She agreed and we made our way back here.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: There were so many paths here, and they're all twisty-turny and up and down... It's hard navigating through them all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did she tell you what's on her mind?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No, she didn't want to talk about that, and I didn't ask. I get the feeling that it'll bring up some unhappy memories.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But if I had to guess, it's probably because she hasn't been able to explore the city for quite some time...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: All she said was that she's sick and doesn't know when she'll get better.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Whenever we passed by busy crowds, she kept turning her head and taking in all the things around her. At first, I thought she was afraid that someone might bump into us...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But when I caught a glimpse in her eyes, I only saw yearning, and a deep sense of loss.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to not be down when something like that happens to you.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: At first, she didn't really want to say anything to me at all — she just gave me yes and no answers.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But what I really saw was just another child, and asked all the same things everyone else did, about rugs, spices, cooking, and the differences between here and home.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Eventually, I think I earned her trust. Hehe, there were many things that she liked in the city after all.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I say that, but honestly, you two probably caught the majority of what she said.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She had already relaxed her guard around you.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Gotta start somewhere. Oh, by the way, did you guys learn anything about the meteor shower?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet we did, big time! You're in luck, Yoimiya — you'll be able to see the meteor shower from Sumeru!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Really!? Haha, that's great! If I had gone looking for it myself, I'm sure I would've missed it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, not necessarily.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Meteor showers appear in response to people's wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: They respond to wishes? Huh. I've never heard that one before...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: So it's not that you wish upon shooting stars, but that wishes summon them?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, in that case, I was born ready! Don't you worry!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you talking about how you want to use the meteor shower as inspiration for fireworks?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: That's why I'm here, but I wouldn't call that my wish. I don't think that alone will call the stars down for us, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah, that makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Wow, she's adding her own spin onto this...)

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then we'll have to "practice" wishing a little.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Can you two come with me? Let me put my thoughts together, and tell me if you understand.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: As for what my wish is... Hehe, it's a secret for now.

choices.text: How about a change of scenery?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and we'll take the opportunity to show you some views you've definitely never seen before!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: More places to see? Alright, let's go!

choices.text: Let's go someplace that better fits the mood.

talks.objective: Leave the Akademiya and talk to Paimon about a plan

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We said we were gonna find someone from Rtawahist, but now that Paimon thinks about it, no one really fits the bill...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, the previous Rtawahist sage was Azar.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Layla's probably having a tough time right now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks Alhaitham might know something, but... Paimon doesn't want to talk to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why don't we just ask around? Maybe we'll run into someone from Rtawahist.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Looks like you two are in a pickle. Why not consult someone who always tells you everything she knows?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida!? Why are you here?

choices.text: Thanks for the scare.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm here to meet with some researchers, but when I saw you two looking so troubled, I decided to follow.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Looks like I showed up just in time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, we might as well tell you. We have a friend who's come to Sumeru...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Nahida about Yoimiya and the meteor shower.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hm, I see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, your face says that it's gonna be a long time before the next meteor shower...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Um... My answer is going to be even more of a disappointment.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You may have heard that the stars are related to people's fates.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, lots of times.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If the stars dictate destiny, then do you think that destiny is something that is unchanging and always follows predicted outcomes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have a point...

choices.text: If that were so...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: According to current Rtawahist research, a meteor shower is a celestial phenomenon that occurs due to the interference between many intricate fates.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Their appearance is highly random. Some have tried coming up with ways to predict their occurrence, but the results are less than reliable.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This is a far cry from folktales that claim meteor showers "come at certain times" and "bless all who witness them."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you mean we won't be able to see one?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm sorry to disappoint you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we tell this to Yoimiya, she'll be so disappointed...

choices.text: She's been so excited this entire time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What now? There has to be something we can do...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Yoimiya's always genuine with everyone, and she does her best to protect the dreams of children.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Just like the time she hung out with the kids on the beach and talked with them about the Great Mujina Youkai.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And now, when she's the one who wants to see something, her fire has to be extinguished like this...)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Are you two okay? It seems the news hit harder than I expected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon just thinks this isn't fair to Yoimiya.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Good people should be repaid for their good deeds.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I get it. From how you described her, I can see that she is a kind and caring soul...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So why don't we take a page out of her book and protect her dreams with a well-intentioned "lie"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? How do we do that?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It'll be a story about a meteor shower. You'll accompany her on a brief journey, do a bit of work here and there, and then receive the meteor shower as a reward.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, I can't summon a real meteor shower, but if it's in a dream, I can help out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That would be great, Nahida!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you so much.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Compared to what you've done for me, this is nothing.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Use the meteor shower as a pretext to take Yoimiya all around Sumeru. Then, when you're ready, blow this.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'll tell the Aranara in advance. Once they hear the whole story, I'm sure they'll be willing to help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm, then the dream will probably be like the one we had in the Avidya Forest, when we first met Haypasia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was a real shocker! It was hard to tell that we were even in a dream.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, only later did we realize that.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Once the meteor shower ends and you all awaken from the dream, she'll probably realize what had happened.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If you tell her the truth at that point, she should be a lot less disappointed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm, Paimon thinks this is the best way to simulate the meteor shower. Thanks, Nahida!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, you're welcome. I'm glad I could help.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Still, you two should get the story straight before you join up with your friend. If not, she's gonna see right through everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True. Let's discuss it on the way!

choices.text: This was a rare trip abroad for her.
Rtawahist would have achieved one of their ultimate goals.
Right on cue.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Stay safe and have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: Thanks for your patronage. Hope you enjoy them!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I won't go too far, and don't worry about me getting bored. I'm an expert at finding ways to pass time!

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: (Business today is pretty good. I'll check the books later...)

dialogues.speaker: Fayez
dialogues.text: (I wonder what other Inazumans would think of the Aranara Carvings...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's about it for Port Ormos. Next up is Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Alright. Let's get to it!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: (What to do first... Hmm, maybe I'll see what they're selling around here.)
